doc.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020

title: Tribute recording of the Bob Newhart theme for Pat Williams
summary: Bergeron describes his new recording of 'The Bob Newhart Theme' arranged by Tom Kubis and why the melody mattered to him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I just did a — I’ll share a little something with you when we — after we hang up. I did a tribute recording to him that I just mixed and mastered. I did “The Bob Newhart Theme.” And I had Tom Kubis do a really nice arrangement of it, and I’ve got strings on it and everything. And I’ll send it to you. It’s going to get released on January 1 as a matter of fact, just as a little single. And I did it for Pat’s wife, so I’m going to send it to her.
Okay. I got to play that theme, he came to Utica, New York.
I was in the group so I got to play that theme.

Yeah I did an HBO special for Bob Newhart, you know, thirty years ago probably. And I’ve always loved that — that’s a theme that’s always stuck with me, and that [scats] Buddy Childers, you know, played that beautiful soaring trumpet. And from the time I was a kid I always liked that. That melody has been in my head, and so when I started working for Pat, you know, I was like so excited to be playing for him and so I decided to record that and just get it off my chest after all these years you know.
